issues.legal_issue: A tenancy created by a mortgagee in possession does not bind the mortgagor after redemption when the mortgage deed does not provide for the tenancy to continue and the lease is neither approved by the mortgagor nor an act of prudent management.
material_facts: A mortgagee in possession leased an urban shop to the occupants after a prior tenant vacated.
The mortgage deed directed the mortgagee to enjoy the property by collecting rent, but did not authorize a tenancy to continue after redemption.
The court found no approval or concurrence by the mortgagor for the occupants to remain after redemption.
The High Court found that inducting the occupants was not an act of prudent management.
The owner’s successor and a subsequent mortgagee sued to redeem the mortgage and recover possession.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy created by the mortgagee did not bind the mortgagor after redemption, and the occupants were liable to surrender possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 60, 76(a), and 111(c) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, redemption restores the mortgagor’s independent right, and interests created by the mortgagee generally cease with the mortgage. A lease may bind the mortgagor after redemption where the lease specifically and categorically provides for continuation and is an act of prudent management, or where the mortgagor approved or concurred in it. The Court followed Jadavji Purshottam v. Dhani Navnitbhai Amaratlal and Pomal Kanji Govindji v. Vrajlal Karsandas Purohit.

rule.if: redemption_suit and tenant_inducted_by_mortgagee and deed_lacks_survival_term and not mortgagor_approved_continuation and not prudent_management_lease

predicates.redemption_suit: The proceeding seeks redemption of a mortgage and recovery of the mortgaged property.
predicates.tenant_inducted_by_mortgagee: A mortgagee in possession put a tenant into possession of the property.
predicates.deed_lacks_survival_term: The mortgage instrument does not provide that a tenancy created by the mortgagee will continue after redemption.
predicates.mortgagor_approved_continuation: The mortgagor approved or concurred in the tenant’s continuing in possession after redemption.
predicates.prudent_management_lease: The lease was an act of prudent management by the mortgagee.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding concerns a tenant inducted by the mortgagee, and the deed does not provide for continuation, the mortgagor did not approve continuation, and the lease was not prudent management, the tenancy does not bind the mortgagor after redemption.

issues.legal_issue: Rent-control protection against eviction does not prevent recovery of possession from a tenant inducted by a mortgagee when the person redeeming the mortgage was never the tenant’s landlord.
material_facts: The occupants were inducted as tenants by the mortgagee, not by the owner or the owner’s successor seeking possession.
The suit sought redemption of the mortgage and recovery of possession from the occupants.
The Court found that there had never been a landlord-tenant relationship between the occupants and the person seeking possession.
issues.conclusion: The rent-control statute did not bar execution of the decree for possession because the occupants were not tenants of the person seeking possession.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(3), 2(6), and 11(1) of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, protect a tenant from eviction except in accordance with the Act, but the non obstante protection applies to a decree obtained by a landlord against a tenant. It did not apply here because the occupants were never tenants of the person redeeming the mortgage. The Court distinguished Raj Brij Raj Krishna v. S.K. Shaw & Bros., M/s. Raval & Co. v. K.G. Ramachandran, V. Dhanpal Chettiar v. Yesodai Ammal, Gian Devi Anand v. Jeevan Kumar, and G. Ponniah Thevar v. Nalleyam Perumal Pillai.

predicates.redemption_suit: The proceeding seeks redemption of a mortgage and recovery of the mortgaged property.
predicates.tenant_inducted_by_mortgagee: A mortgagee in possession put a tenant into possession of the property.
predicates.no_tenancy_relationship_with_person_seek: The person seeking possession was never the tenant’s landlord.

issues.definition: In a mortgage-redemption proceeding, rent-control protection does not bar recovery of possession from a tenant inducted by the mortgagee when the person seeking possession was never that tenant’s landlord.
